note: Migrations that read a column only SOME definitions of a multiply-defined table have. D1 keeps one table per name and every definition is CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, so the first file to run won and the rest were no-ops; a migration naming a column from the losing shape cannot apply at all. Migration 196 is why this check exists — it named quotes.partner_id and service_offerings.owner_user_id, which come from opposite lineages, so no ordering of those files could satisfy both. It failed its first production run and D1 rolled it back. Empty is the correct state: an entry here is a migration that will fail against at least one possible database, so prefer fixing the migration to recording it.
resolve_with: npx wrangler d1 execute studioos-db --remote --command="PRAGMA table_info('<table>')"
